To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) ads with implicit intent are more effective when they are presented during the predecisional stage, (b) the effect of advertising intent is moderated by brand image, and (c) ads with weak brand image are more effective in the predecision stage.

the timing of ad exposure (pre- vs. post-decisional) interacts with the advertising intent (implicit vs. explicit) and the brand image (weak vs. strong) to impact the effectiveness of online interruption-based ads.

Online ads shown in the decision-making phase are more effective for weak brands with implicit advertising intent, while ads shown in the postdecisional stage are more effective for strong brands with explicit advertising intent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a better understanding of online interruption-based advertising, a phenomenon that has received relatively little attention in the literature.
the design principles of interruption-based advertising in online retailing.
understanding the design factors and their interrelationships that are critical to the success of interruption-based advertising.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the timing of the ad, the intent of the ad and the image of the brand are all factors that affect the effectiveness of online pop-up advertisements.
the effects of advertising design on consumer response are contingent upon the context in which the ads are shown.
the timing of the ad, the intent of the ad, and the brand image all interact to affect purchase intention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
online interruption-based ads are more effective when the ads are designed with implicit intent and shown in the pre-decisional shopping phase.
the effectiveness of online interruption-based advertising depends on the interplay between exposure timing, advertising content, and brand image.

the effectiveness of online interruption-based ads is contingent on the design of ad content (i.e., advertising intent) and ad exposure (i.e., timing of exposure) in relation to the consumer's stage of the shopping journey.
The main takeaway from our work is that
online interruption-based ads should be designed with implicit advertising intention and launched in predecisional phase for weak brands.
the design of online interruption-based ads should be carefully considered to achieve the intended advertising effects.
the timing of online interruption-based advertising can influence consumers' responses, and the impact of timing is contingent on advertising intent and brand image.
